files.lesson.md: --- order: 9 unit: powers9 node: AC9M9A01 n3 uses: [AC9M9A01 n2] assumes: [AC9M8N02 n1, AC9M8N02 n2] connection: scale-up-monster title: Index laws with letters summary: "A letter stands for a number, so the index laws work on it the same way. Numbers in front multiply; indices add, subtract or multiply by the same laws." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Make an animal 10 times longer, and how much heavier does it get? Letters and index laws can tell you." app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8346 url: http://127.0.0.1:8346/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: laws.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$a^2 \\times a^3$: two $a$s and three $a$s make five, so $a^5$. Here $a = 3$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@laws.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "A letter follows the same laws as a number" say: "A letter is a number you haven't chosen yet. The same laws work." clip: - caption: { text: "a² × a¹: three a's in all: a³.", say: "A squared times a: three a's, so a cubed." } - click: Make the second index bigger - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "a² × a²: four a's: a⁴. The indices add.", say: "Two and two: four a's. The indices add." } - click: Make the second index bigger - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "a² × a³: five a's: a⁵.", say: "Two and three make five." } - wait: 800 --- A letter is just a number you haven't chosen yet. So the index laws you know work on it, with the numbers in front kept separate. ## Predict: the scaled-up lizard ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a weight for the scaled-up lizard shows who thinks weight grows with length (×10) or with area (×100) rather than volume." check: type: predict q: "A film monster is a lizard made 10 times longer, 10 times wider and 10 times taller, in the same shape. How many times heavier is it?" options: - "1000 times" - "10 times" - "100 times" - "30 times" actual: "1000 times. Weight follows volume: length × width × height. 10 × 10 × 10 = 10³ = 1000. Its leg bones only get 10 × 10 = 100 times the cross-section, so each part of a leg carries 10 times as much as before." ``` A lizard is scaled up 10 times in every direction. Is its weight 10 times, 100 times or 1000 times more? ## Run: add the indices ```step stage: run insight: "Multiplying powers of the same base adds the indices, whatever the base. A letter is a base you haven't chosen yet." try: { playground: board, starter: "laws.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Set the board to $a^2 \\times a^3$ with $a = 3$. How many $a$s are there in all?", when: "a = 3 and m = 2 and n = 3" } ``` Change the base and the indices. The board uses a number for $a$. The laws are the same for any $a$. ## Investigate: numbers and letters ```step stage: investigate insight: "Coefficients multiply and powers of each letter follow the index laws. Kim multiplies the indices when she should add them." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Simplify $a^3 \\times a^5$. Type $a^8$ as a^8." answer: "a^8" form: simplified feedback: - ["a^15", "Multiplying powers adds the indices: 3 + 5, not 3 × 5."] - ["2a^8", "There's no 2: a³ × a⁵ is eight a's multiplied."] explain: "a³ × a⁵: three a's and five a's make eight: a⁸." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#kim" text: "Kim simplifies $3a^2 \\times 4a^3$. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: index-multiply-for-product explain: "Line 3: multiplying powers adds the indices: 2 + 3 = 5. So 3a² × 4a³ = 12a⁵." - check: type: question q: "What is $(2a^3)^2$?" options: ["$4a^6$", "$2a^6$", "$4a^5$", "$2a^5$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The 2 is squared too: 2 × 2 = 4.", "A power of a power multiplies: 3 × 2 = 6.", "Square the 2 and multiply the indices."] explain: "(2a³)² = 2² × (a³)² = 4a⁶." ``` ### Add the indices Here's the routine with numbers and two letters. ```worked 3x^2y \times 4xy^3 \div 6x^2y :: Numbers, then each letter. = 12x^3y^4 \div 6x^2y :: Multiply: 3 × 4 = 12, x² × x = x³, y × y³ = y⁴. = 2 x^{3-2} y^{4-1} :: Divide: 12 ÷ 6 = 2, subtract the indices. = 2xy^3 :: x¹ is just x. ``` Now try one on paper: $5a^3b^2 \times 2ab^4$. Then type your answer. ### Find the mistake Read Kim's working. Add or multiply? ### A power of a product ## Modify: change the letters and indices ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing the pattern: a smaller index on top (a negative result), a power of a power and a zero index." try: { playground: board, starter: "laws.yml#vary", height: 620 } tasks: - hint: ["Set m to 2 and n to 5.", "Subtract the indices: 2 − 5."] check: { type: answer, q: "Simplify $a^2 \\div a^5$. Type $a^{-3}$ as a^-3.", answer: "a^-3", form: simplified, feedback: [["a^3", "2 − 5 is −3, not 3."], ["-a^3", "A negative index doesn't make a negative number."]], explain: "a² ÷ a⁵ = a^(2−5) = a⁻³." } smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Just the index: what's $2 - 5$?", answer: -3, explain: "2 − 5 = −3." } - hint: ["Do the power of a power first.", "$(a^2)^3 = a^6$."] check: { type: answer, q: "Simplify $(a^2)^3 \\times a$.", answer: "a^7", form: simplified, feedback: [["a^6", "There's an extra a: a⁶ × a¹."], ["a^5", "Multiply the indices in the brackets: 2 × 3 = 6."]], explain: "(a²)³ = a⁶, and a⁶ × a = a⁷." } - hint: ["Anything to the power 0 is 1.", "$(7a)^0$ means the whole bracket."] check: { type: number, q: "Edge case: what is $(7a)^0$? (Take $a$ as any number that isn't 0.)", answer: 1, explain: "Anything (not zero) to the power 0 is 1." } ``` ### Smaller on top ### A power of a power ### Zero index ## Practise: mixed laws with letters ```step stage: practise insight: "Using each law with letters, coefficients and two letters, mixed; the review keeps a numeric negative power fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Simplify $6x^4 \\times 2x^3$." answer: "12x^7" form: simplified feedback: - ["12x^12", "Multiplying powers adds the indices: 4 + 3."] - ["8x^7", "Multiply the numbers: 6 × 2 = 12."] explain: "6 × 2 = 12 and x⁴ × x³ = x⁷." - check: type: answer q: "Simplify $10a^7b^2 \\div 5a^3b$." answer: "2a^4b" form: simplified feedback: - ["2a^10b", "Dividing powers subtracts the indices: 7 − 3 = 4."] - ["5a^4b", "10 ÷ 5 = 2."] explain: "10 ÷ 5 = 2, a⁷ ÷ a³ = a⁴, b² ÷ b = b." - check: type: answer q: "Simplify $(3a^2)^3$." answer: "27a^6" form: simplified feedback: - ["3a^6", "The 3 is cubed too: 27."] - ["9a^6", "3³ = 27, not 9."] explain: "3³ = 27 and (a²)³ = a⁶." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Just the number: what's $3^3$?", answer: 27, explain: "3 × 3 × 3 = 27." } - check: type: answer q: "Review: work out $4^{-2}$ as a fraction." answer: "1/16" form: simplest feedback: - ["-16", "A negative power isn't a negative number."] explain: "4⁻² = 1/4² = 1/16." ``` ### Multiply ### Divide ### A power of a product ### Review A negative power, from the last two lessons. ## Make: back to the monster ```step stage: make insight: "Coming back to the lizard: letters let the scaling work for any factor, and the ratio shows why the legs struggle." tasks: - hint: ["Scale factor k: length k, area k², volume k³.", "Divide weight by leg area."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A lizard is made $k$ times longer in every direction. Its weight goes up by $k^3$ and the cross-section of its legs by $k^2$. By what factor does the load on each bit of leg go up, when $k = 10$?" steps: - ["Weight $\\times k^3$ and leg area $\\times k^2$", "what grows by how much"] - ["$k^3 \\div k^2 = k$", "subtract the indices"] - ["$k = 10$: ten times", "put the scale factor in"] answer: "10" answerLabel: "Load on each bit of leg (times)" feedback: - ["1000", "That's the weight. Divide by the leg area's 100."] - ["100", "That's the leg area. The load is weight ÷ area."] criteria: - "I wrote the weight and the leg area using k." - "I subtracted the indices when I divided." - "My answer goes up with k." explain: "k³ ÷ k² = k: ten times the load on each bit of leg." - check: type: question q: "Which grows fastest when a shape is scaled up by $k$?" options: ["Volume, $k^3$", "Area, $k^2$", "Length, $k$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Area grows by k², but volume grows by k³, faster.", "Length grows the slowest."] explain: "Volume goes with k³, which grows fastest." ``` ### The legs Back to the lizard. Work it out on paper first, then type your answer. ### What grows fastest? The scaling facts here come from the geometry of similar shapes. Real animals aren't exact copies at different sizes, so this is a model, not a measurement. **Also used in** - **Science.** Why small animals can jump many times their length and big ones can't. - **Next lesson.** Writing very big and very small numbers in scientific notation. ```teacher summary: "Students apply the index laws to letters: coefficients multiply, indices add, subtract or multiply, and a scaled-up lizard shows weight and leg strength growing at different rates (AC9M9A01, node 3)." time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can simplify products and quotients of powers of letters. - I can deal with the number in front separately from the letters. - I can explain why volume grows faster than area. struggle: Keeping coefficients and indices apart. Ask students to circle the numbers in front and simplify them first. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need All the index laws. The one idea: a letter is a number, so the same laws work; coefficients are multiplied or divided on their own. The common mistake is multiplying indices for a product (Kim's working). The lizard is a model: similar shapes scale as k, k² and k³. Real animals change shape as they get bigger. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Those who chose 100 times used area, not volume." - "Run: ask students to say how many a's there are before reading the index." - "Paper: the try-one after the worked example and the leg load in Make are worked on paper first. Books out, and look for the numbers worked out separately." - "Modify: before a² ÷ a⁵, ask whether the answer is bigger or smaller than 1." stuck: - see: A student writes 3a² × 4a³ = 12a⁶. ask: How many a's are there in all? fix: "Five: a² is two a's and a³ is three. 12a⁵." - see: A student writes (3a²)³ = 3a⁶. ask: Which part is cubed? fix: "The whole bracket: 3³ = 27 as well." stretch: Why can an ant carry many times its own weight but an elephant can't? Use k³ ÷ k². support: A card with the three laws and a worked example with numbers and letters side by side. leads: > Continues AC9M9A01 node 3. Where it leads: scientific notation (next), area and volume scaling, exponential functions (Year 10). exit: q: Simplify 8x⁵ ÷ 2x². a: 4x³. explain: > A letter stands for a number, so the index laws work on it. Multiplying adds the indices, dividing subtracts them, and a power of a power multiplies them. Numbers in front multiply or divide on their own: $3a^2 \times 4a^3 = 12a^5$. ```

# Kim's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: kim
Simplify 3a² × 4a³.
Multiply the numbers: 3 × 4 = 12.
Multiply the powers of a: 2 × 3 = 6.
So 3a² × 4a³ = 12a⁶.
